The Lean plan passed structural validation and independent fidelity review; proof construction is still pending. Round A asks whether to build three cited results in your private toolkit before the paper's proofs. I checked the annotated manuscript passages and the primary sources; all three independent checker receipts agree, with no duplicate identified.

1. Gaussian covariance bound for cross-dependent quadratic forms — Bellec (2023), Lemma 7.1, equations (7.2)-(7.3). It bounds covariance of quadratic errors with coefficients depending on the other Gaussian vector; useful for rowwise risk-error control. The proposed generic statement keeps all four moment conditions and constant 4. Recommendation: defer.

2. Gaussian divergence bound for a product of vector fields — Bellec and Shen (2022), proof of Proposition 14, equation (C.3). It controls bilinear Gaussian estimation errors through field sizes and derivatives; the proposed statement keeps factor 2 and finite right-hand moments. Recommendation: defer.

3. Second-order Gaussian divergence bound for a bounded vector field — Bellec and Shen (2022), proof of Proposition 16, equation (C.6). It approximates squared divergences by dimension times field energy; the proposed statement keeps the unit bound and dimension-uniform constant. Recommendation: defer.

All three are first-sighting Tricks entries with no recorded recurrence. The PaperFormalizer skill requires defer recommendations for that category and reserves each toolkit promotion decision to you. Deferring all three continues the paper's Lean proofs with these inequalities explicitly recorded as cited assumptions. Building all three first attempts to prove and review the external inequalities too and can take substantially longer. You can choose individually on this page, accept all recorded recommendations, or tell me to defer all three / build all three in the Codex session. Which choice do you want?
